post.description: Discover the CRM's record types (Person, Company, Deal, Project and any imported ones) and the fields you may read. The organisation is fixed by the server; never ask the person to choose one. Use before filtering or writing unfamiliar fields.

Find CRM records you may read, with equality filters and pagination. Each result has a stable id, revision and href. Link an entity in a workspace page with its href ([Name](/crm?record=<id>)) instead of copying its fields into the page. In a conversation other people read, only records every participant can read are listed.

Read one record: permitted fields, sources, links, pending proposals, the workspaces bound to it, and 'mentioned_in' — the pages that link it, only from workspaces you are a member of. A merged id answers the surviving record. If this is refused with reason shared_conversation, say you cannot use it here and offer the person's private chat. Read before changing a record.

Create a record, change one, propose a change, or merge a duplicate into the record that survives. As an agent your changes are PROPOSALS: the result says status 'proposed', and a person accepts or rejects them on the record page — tell them it is waiting and give the record link. Updates need the revision crm_read returned; include a reason and source evidence (a meeting id, a page). Create needs an idempotency_key.
Read up to 100 recent revisions of a record. Your current access filters historical values too.

Accept or reject a pending proposal — for a person with review rights using their own credential. An agent is refused with reason person_confirmation_required: point the person at the record page instead. Acceptance conflicts if the record changed since the proposal.

Read or configure a shared per-type card layout (CRM administrators). Omit layout to read its version; send a layout with expected_version and reason to save. Sections reference real fields; formats are text, markdown, number, currency, percent, date or badge. This changes presentation, never record values or access.

Bind a workspace to a record, or remove the binding (CRM administrators). Members of a bound workspace may then read the record, and its contributors and owners may change it; the grant ends when their membership does. A page linking a record grants nothing — only a binding does. Confirm with the person in one sentence before binding.

Read the person's own desktop: its version, its layout (sections in order with hidden, collapsed, column, span and size; item order; grouping; filters), the agents and files placed on it, pending suggestions and saved arrangements. Read it before arranging, and pass its version as base_version.

Change the person's desktop directly — ONLY when the person asked for this in the current turn ("put agents first", "hide files", "place my pricing notes"). Then reply in one line saying what changed and that Undo is on the desktop. If you were not asked in this turn, or you run in a routine, on an event, or in a chat other people share, you are refused with propose_instead: call desktop_arrange_propose instead. Refused with desk_changed: read again and retry once on the new version.

Suggest a desktop arrangement the person did not ask for in this turn. It waits on their desktop with your one-line reason beside Apply and Not now; nothing changes until they apply it. Suggest sparingly: at most 5 wait per person and each session may suggest 20 a day. Tell the person in one line that a suggestion is waiting.
The person applies or dismisses a desktop suggestion, with their own credential (a confirmation, not a tool).
Restore an earlier desktop version, layout and placements, as a new version (the desktop's Undo).

Read the person's own settings for their workspaces: pinned, hidden from home, muted, room_order, level and collapsed sections, keyed by workspace slug. Only workspaces the person changed are listed; any other reads as the defaults (not pinned, not hidden, not muted, no order, no level, nothing collapsed). They are private to the person and say nothing about who else is in a workspace.

Change the person's own settings for one workspace — ONLY when the person asked for it in this turn ("mute Growth", "pin Product planning to the top", "hide Old archive from my home"). Send only the keys that change; the answer is the full settings after the change. Then reply in one line saying what changed. Settings grant no access and share nothing. In a routine, on an event, or in a chat other people share you are refused with person_only: tell the person in one line how to do it themselves.

List cards: a workspace's board (the cards it references), the person's own (mine), or both by default; filter by about or stage. Each card has its stage, what's next, who it waits on, its sub-cards and members, and its revision. Also lists the proposals waiting for this person's answer. Read before proposing, so you do not propose a card that exists.

Propose a new card — a shared, Trello-like card in the organisation's registry: a title, what it is about, a stage, what's next. It lands as a proposal: on the person's own desktop, or on a workspace's board (one you work in) for its members; a person adds it or says not now. You never make a card yourself. Give a one-line reason. Tell the person in one line that it is waiting.

Propose a change to a card: its fields (Next, Waiting, Summary, Due, Progress, Checklist, Title), its face, or a stage move (`transition`). A member accepts it; a stage never moves without a person. Pass the card's current revision and a one-line reason, and tell the person in one line that it is waiting.

One card for the person, with its activity (its movement history). Reading never marks it
seen; the terminal does, on render in view (/card/seen).

The person's Inbox: open cards whose next actor they are, and the counts the Now strip,
the Inbox and a room badge read (one predicate).
The terminal rendered the card in view (D14): the only writer of `seen`. Session credential only.
A server nonce bound to this person, this card at its revision and the face they see (D13).

A gate decision on a card (D12) by its next actor, recorded as a decision record (D13):
session credential, the nonce, and the content hash of the face they saw. Never an agent.
The person makes a card ("Make a card"), with their own credential. An agent is refused with propose_instead.
A member changes a card or moves its stage, with their own credential.
A member adds a person to a card (they are invited, and decide) or removes one; anyone may leave.
The person added to a card accepts or declines.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: Workspace slug whose members get derived grants on the record.

nonce.title: Nonce
nonce.description: From POST /card/nonce, minted for this person and this face.

content_hash.title: Content Hash
content_hash.description: The content hash /card/nonce answered: the face the person saw.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: A workspace's board: the cards it references.

mine.title: Mine
mine.description: Only cards the person is a member of.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: The person id to add (invited) or remove.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: The workspace whose board it goes on — one you work in. Omit for the person's own card.

about.title: About
about.description: What the card is about, as a reference: page:<workspace>/<path>, chat:<id>, workspace:<slug>, meeting:<id> or crm:<record id>. Members of the card never get access to it through the card.

type.title: Type
type.description: A card type; Card unless the company declared others.

parent.title: Parent
parent.description: Make it a sub-card of this card id.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Optional card fields: Next (what happens next, <=200), Waiting (who or what it waits on), Summary (<=500), Due (YYYY-MM-DD), Progress (0..1), Checklist ([{text, done}] <=10), Title. Never State: a stage moves with `transition`. AN OBLIGATION (D11): Kind (commitment | approval | question | ask | invitation | policy_change) with NextActor (the person id whose move it is — required with a Kind), Requester (the person id waiting on it; defaults to the person you act for), Due, Origin (session:<id> or message:<session>/<message id>) and Chain ({blocks: [card ids], blocked_by: [card ids]}). A card with a Kind is OFFERED to its next actor at once and only that person moves it.

face.title: Face
face.description: Optional face: up to 8 blocks. Structural: {type: stepper|people|movement|waiting|next|subcards|ref|status}. Data blocks NAME a field and never carry a value: {type: metric|text|progress|due|checklist|list, field: '<card field>', label?: '<=40 chars'}. To say something on the face, put it in a field (Next, Summary) and show that field. Unknown blocks are dropped.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One line the person reads beside Add / Not now: why this card.

expected_revision.title: Expected Revision
expected_revision.description: The revision card_list or the card returned.

AN OBLIGATION (D11): Kind (commitment | approval | question | ask | invitation | policy_change) with NextActor (the person id whose move it is — required with a Kind), Requester (the person id waiting on it; defaults to the person you act for), Due, Origin (session:<id> or message:<session>/<message id>) and Chain ({blocks: [card ids], blocked_by: [card ids]}). A card with a Kind is OFFERED to its next actor at once and only that person moves it.

Data blocks NAME a field and never carry a value: {type: metric|text|progress|due|checklist|list, field: '<card field>', label?: '<=40 chars'}. transition.title: Transition
transition.description: Move the card to this stage of its lifecycle (one of the card's states or side_states). Always a proposal a person accepts.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One line the person reads: why this change.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Required for create: stable caller-generated key reused when retrying the same request.

into.title: Into
into.description: For merge: the record that survives. The merged record_id then answers this one everywhere.

match.title: Match
match.description: For create: match identifiers — email:a@b.c, domain:b.c, calendar:<event id>. One identifier belongs to one record; a clash means search or merge, never a second record.

narrative.title: Narrative
narrative.description: Native Markdown description of this CRM record. Supports headings, lists, tables, workspace links and stable [label](/crm?record=UUID) links. Stable CRM links are indexed as relationships with backlinks. Search for mentioned people, companies and products first and link verified matches by their href; never invent identities, facts or URLs. Null preserves the description; empty string clears it. Requires current revision and reason.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: Card layout: {title_field: 'Name', sections: [{title: 'Overview', fields: [{field: 'Amount', label: 'Investment', format: 'currency', currency: 'USD'}]}], show_narrative: true, show_related: true}. Field formats: text, markdown, number, currency, percent (0..100), date, badge.

object_type.title: Object Type
object_type.description: Optional object type; omit to discover permitted object types.

ops.title: Ops
ops.description: 1..50 declarative operations on the person's own desktop, applied in order; a bad one refuses the whole list. Sections: workspaces, agents, files, cards. Refs: agent:<routine id>, chat:<chat session id> (a chat, drawn in agents), file:<workspace slug>/<path>, workspace:<slug> (ordering only; workspaces are never placed). {op:'order',section,ids:[refs]} · {op:'move',id,before|after} (a ref within its section, or a section id among sections) · {op:'group',section,by:'workspace'|'type'|'state'|'about'} or {op:'group',section,named:[{title,ids}]} · {op:'show'|'hide'|'collapse'|'expand'|'section_top',section} · {op:'section_order',sections:[…]} · {op:'section_place',section,column:1..3,span?:1..3,side_by_side_with?} · {op:'section_size',section,size:'compact'|'normal'|'tall'} · {op:'place'|'remove',ref} (an agent, a chat or a file this person can read; it never creates, edits or shares anything) · {op:'filter',section,where:'<predicate>'|null,until?:'<ISO time>'} · {op:'save',name} · {op:'restore',name}.

base_version.title: Base Version
base_version.description: The version desktop_read returned. A different current version is refused with desk_changed: read again.

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional: save the resulting arrangement under this name, to restore later.

ops.title: Ops
ops.description: 1..50 declarative operations on the person's own desktop, applied in order; a bad one refuses the whole list. Sections: workspaces, agents, files, cards. Refs: agent:<routine id>, chat:<chat session id> (a chat, drawn in agents), file:<workspace slug>/<path>, workspace:<slug> (ordering only; workspaces are never placed). {op:'order',section,ids:[refs]} · {op:'move',id,before|after} (a ref within its section, or a section id among sections) · {op:'group',section,by:'workspace'|'type'|'state'|'about'} or {op:'group',section,named:[{title,ids}]} · {op:'show'|'hide'|'collapse'|'expand'|'section_top',section} · {op:'section_order',sections:[…]} · {op:'section_place',section,column:1..3,span?:1..3,side_by_side_with?} · {op:'section_size',section,size:'compact'|'normal'|'tall'} · {op:'place'|'remove',ref} (an agent, a chat or a file this person can read; it never creates, edits or shares anything) · {op:'filter',section,where:'<predicate>'|null,until?:'<ISO time>'} · {op:'save',name} · {op:'restore',name}.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One line the person reads beside Apply / Not now: why this arrangement helps them.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version to restore (undo_version from the last change); 0 is the default desktop.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Equality filters on readable fields; discover field names with crm_describe.

pinned.title: Pinned
pinned.description: Pin the workspace to the top of the home.

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description: Hide it from the person's home (it stays open to them).

muted.title: Muted
muted.description: Mute it: no notifications from it.

notify.title: Notify
notify.description: RETIRED: refused. The notification level lives in the person's identity notification policy (Settings → Notifications).

room_order.title: Room Order
room_order.description: Chat ids in the person's order (at most 100).

level.title: Level
level.description: The person's level override for this workspace, 1..5; null follows their default.

collapsed.title: Collapsed
collapsed.description: Section ids the person collapsed (at most 20).

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: The workspace slug; 'personal' is the person's own.

settings.description: Only the keys to change; the rest stay as they are.
